what: Cover scene of the Workshop 3 progress deck (https://claude.ai/artifact/8o2ZFe8tHr5Z4yojpAoNvC), 22 Nov 2026. New scene type: a roadside milestone; Zholdas plants a small red pennant and looks at the viewer (the cover).

cover-milestone.jpg.scene: a roadside milestone on an Alpine hillside; Zholdas plants a red pennant and looks at the viewer

letters-postbox.jpg.scene: a red postbox by a country road; Zholdas slips a stack of letters into it, looking at the slot
letters-postbox.jpg.status: replaced on 22 Nov by postbox-corner.webp: the owner did not want the scene boxed inside a card

paint-lane-corner.webp.scene: a road growing from the right and bottom edges, transparent elsewhere, the left edge feathered; Zholdas paints a fresh white lane line (work in progress)

before-after-band.jpg.scene: one continuous valley, 21:9: on the left Zholdas squints into fog with an old phone; on the right, in sun, Zholdas reads a radar screen; train and ferry in view. Neither looks at the viewer.

empty-mailbox.jpg.scene: the gate of a trucking yard; Zholdas peers into an empty mailbox, scratching his cap, his own letters at his feet

farewell-buffer-stop.jpg.scene: the end of a railway siding at dusk: Zholdas rests on the grass against a red buffer stop with a cup of tea, a thermos beside him, and looks at the viewer (the finale); resting freight wagons, a small truck by a warehouse, the Alps. The first version, lifting his cap, was dropped by the owner.

next-fork-signpost.jpg.scene: a fork in a country road with a blank signpost: Zholdas, seen from behind, looks up at the arrows with a map, scratching his cap; one road to a town with a rail yard, the other to an Alpine valley with trucks. The question slide: which way to reach companies.

postbox-corner.webp.slide: validation, bottom-right corner under the Bocconi outreach card
postbox-corner.webp.scene: transparent everywhere except the bottom-right: a grassy verge and a country road grow from the right and bottom edges; Zholdas on tiptoe slips letters into a red postbox, looking at the slot; bundles at his feet; a small van leaves through the right edge. The verge ends in a soft hill line, no straight cut.
